NO. 047 · The Kingfishers / Alcedinidae · Kingfishers

Common Kingfisher

普通翠鸟 · pǔ tōng cuì niǎo Alcedo atthis
Resident Common 16–17 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A blue bolt that flies just above the water

Cobalt blue and burnt orange, two colours collided, small as a flying jewel. It sits on a low twig staring at the water, then stabs into it and comes back to the same perch with a fish — the whole thing takes under two seconds.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • UpperpartsCrown, back and wings brilliant blue-green with a metallic sheen; a bright blue stripe runs down the centre of the back.
  • UnderpartsBreast and belly orange-red, throat white, ear-coverts orange-red, a small white patch on the chin.
  • BillBlack, long and dagger-sharp; the female's lower mandible is orange-red at the base — 'lipstick' — while the male's is all black.
  • ShapeShort and compact, big head, short tail, very short legs — often bunched into a 'blue ball'.

Behaviour

A classic ambush fisher: it perches one or two metres above the water on a low branch, rock or railing, watches for a long time, then plunges in and returns to the same spot to beat the fish against the perch before swallowing it. Strongly territorial and aggressive towards other kingfishers. It tunnels into earth banks and riverbanks to nest, the tunnel sometimes a metre long.

Voice

A sharp, short 'chee' or 'cheee', high and thin, often given two or three times in flight — an important clue to the bird's presence.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qianshan River
  • Xiangshan Lake Park
  • Qi'ao Island creeks
  • Doumen fish ponds
Field note
Hear that thin high 'chee'? Follow the water to the low branches. It returns to the same perch again and again, so five or ten minutes of patience usually buys you one plunge.
